Revert "Replace default channel"

This reverts commit 911026675de169aee273864b77e122545ad3cde9.

This release was a significant security issue without coordination with
the default channel owner, and thus has to be reverted.

Fix PyPiClient required python version matching

This commit fixes incompatible library versions being selected, due to generator
expression not being rewind after each loop.

Merge pull request #1721 from deathaxe/fix/pypi_client

Fix PyPiClient required python version matching
Fix flake8 errors (#1725)

Reapply "Replace default channel" (#1726)

This reverts commit b56cb2d67b6cd5cf3139e9e2ad9c7efc52b6a456.

Keep current default channel "packages.sublimetext.io" until infrastructure
has been updated.

Current master causes significant degradation of service for many users
as old packagecontrol.io is unmaintained and marked many packages "needs review".

Prepare for python 3.14 (#1714)

This commit fixes library path name and prepares for python 3.14

Fix PEP440Version.is_final for post releases (#1717)

This commit fixes an issue which caust `1.0.post1` not to be treated final.

Fix public events API (#1715)

* Fix public events API

Python 3.13 plugin_host of ST4201+ does no longer support `ZipLoader`.

This commit therefore refactors public `package_control` module to use only
built-in import mechanisms if possible and fallback to `ZipLoader` only,
if a python 3.3 plugin needs to load `events` module from
Package Control.sublime-package running on foreign python 3.8 or 3.13 host.

With this change behavior is equal on all plugin_hosts. Only `events` module
is exported as this is the only module intended to be public.

* Fix __spec__

Remove manipulation of `__spec__.origin` as it is the counter part of `__file__`
but not `__package__`. `__spec__.parent` is derived from `__spec__.name` and
doesn't need to be set.

Fix remove_orphaned_environments typo (#1718)

Fixes #1711

Fix json-schema of repository.json v4.0.0 (#1720)

Package Control 4 requires at least one of "packages", "libraries" or "includes"
keys to be present in repositories.json. This commit fixes jsonschema to create
warnings/errors if "includes" is present, only.

Fix ambiguous git log command line arguments (#1722)

This commit changes command line `git log ..remote/maybe-not-existing-branch`
to `git log -- ..remote/maybe-not-existing-branch` to prevent git
from raising error message about ambiguous arguments, when looking for updates.

This affects upgrading git cloned packages, the tracking remote branch of
a checked out local branch does no longer exist for.

Fix key error caused by version string mangling (#1723)

This commit creates a custom local `Version` from `PEP440Version` to retain
original version string, used for instantiation, in order to use it to access
pypi releases after sorting versions.

That's required because a version string like `str(PEP440Version(2019.09.08))`
returns `2019.1.8`, which then causes `KeyError`, when using it to access
the releases dictionary.

Fix support for backward slash in RECORD files (#1724)

Path elements of file names in RECORD files can be separated by both / and \.

see: https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/recording-installed-packages/#the-record-file

The orjson library is the first one lazily using backslashes for Windows wheels.

Add pymdownx dependency name mapping (#1719)

* Add pymdownx dependency name mapping

Fixes https://github.com/packagecontrol/channel/issues/68

This commit adds a mapping for "pymdownx" dependency name to its official
pypi package "pymdown_extensions".

* Use public visible name as shown in urls

* Add enum dependency mapping

This commit maps `enum` dependency to its official pypi name `enum34`.

see: https://pypi.org/project/enum34/

* Prepare for python 3.14
Re-add support for python 3.13

Sunset legacy dependency format

This commit explicitly removes support for python 3.14 specific dependency
branches in legacy dependencies. Most of them have been migrated to wheels
already.

Bump Version

New version to ensure all clients are updated with reverted channel,
in case those already downloaded reverted v4.2.3

CD: Add manual release workflow

This commit implements a naive manual "Publish Release" workflow,
which just creates a GH release with "Package Control.sublime-package" attached.

Required release steps:

1. update version files
   - package_control/__init__.py
   - package-metadata.json
2. commit as "Bump Version"
3. push to remote
4. run "Publish Release" workflow on GH

The first and only goal is to provide a common public method to do a release,
using trustworthy upstream infrastructure.

Ideas for future changes:

1. trigger when creating semver compliant tags.
2. update version files in repo automatically.
3. auto-create the "Bump Version" commit.
4. maybe auto-sign created package
5. auto-upload to packagecontrol.io/...

ReadMe proofreading (#1729)
Fix typo in cache debug message (#1730)

Fix available libraries listing version (#1733)

This commit adds support for displaying plugin_host specific versions
of available libraries.

Fix modified libraries not being upgraded (#1734)

This commit removes checks to prevent modified libraries from being upgraded.

Originally intended to prevent accidental data loss of in-development libraries
the safe guard may prevent updates in production environments unintentionally.

It is not clear which mechanism modifies files on disk, but users have been
reporting untouched libraries from not upgrading for this reason, repetitively.

Fix curl/wget cacert path (#1735)

Pass ordinary path names to curl/wget as those may not handle 
long UNC path names such as `\\?\C:...` well.

2. uses ST versions to detect supported python version(s), to avoid wrong

Fix order of supported python versions (#1740)

This commit fixes `sys_path.python_versions()` returning supported plugin hosts
in wrong order, causing libraries being installed for wrong hosts.

Remove obsolete import
Add python 3.14 to repository schema (#1742)

Fix removal of locked libraries on Windows (#1741)

This commit moves locked files (e.g. DLLs, pyd) to Data/Trash directory,
to defer removal until next restart of ST, while enabling placing
new file at the same location upon library upgrade.

Technically, charset_normalizer failed to upgrade with WinError 5
due to a .pyd file in Lib/ directory being locked by Windows OS.

The strategy is already used by `delete_directory()` function.

Fix removal of symlinked directories (#1744)

This commit teaches `clear_directory()` function to use `os.unlink` to remove
symlinks on Linux/MacOS.

Note: Modern python raises errors, when calling `os.rmdir()` on symlinks.
